summary:
Eksoterris is an interactive geospatial exploration platform developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Its goal is to identify and investigate locations on Earth with topographic characteristics comparable to lunar and Martian terrain.

The project combines open geospatial datasets, including NASA LOLA, MOLA, and ETOPO1, with Python-based data processing, terrain metrics, and comparative ranking methods to identify potential terrestrial analog candidates.

Through an interactive 3D Earth globe, Moon and Mars models, and a dedicated investigation interface, users can explore candidate locations, compare terrain characteristics, examine independent discovery experiments, and access regional evidence.

The integration with the Gemini API supports structured evidence interpretation while maintaining a clear distinction between measured data, computational results, and information that has not yet been scientifically verified.

Key innovation: transforming complex geospatial data into an interactive research experience that supports the discovery and investigation of potential terrestrial environments for planetary exploration studies.
details:
EKSOTERRIS

Exploring Earth to Better Understand Other Worlds

Project Overview

Eksoterris is an interactive geospatial exploration platform developed by team ICAMIABAS for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. The project aims to identify and investigate terrestrial locations whose topographic characteristics may resemble selected environments on the Moon and Mars.

Problem

Understanding extraterrestrial terrain is challenging because direct access to lunar and Martian environments is limited. Terrestrial analog research can help scientists investigate comparable geological and topographic conditions on Earth, supporting the preparation and study of future planetary exploration activities.

However, identifying potential analog locations requires processing and comparing large amounts of geospatial information from different sources.

Proposed Solution

Eksoterris brings geospatial data acquisition, terrain analysis, comparative screening, and 3D visualization into a single interactive platform.

Users can explore:

  • An interactive 3D Earth globe with terrestrial candidate locations.
  • 3D reference models of the Moon and Mars.
  • Independent candidate discovery experiments.
  • Regional investigation windows and comparative terrain information.
  • Supporting evidence, data sources, and scientific limitations.

Technical Methodology

The platform uses elevation datasets from NASA LOLA, MOLA, and ETOPO1 to investigate terrain characteristics.

Its comparative methodology includes:

  • P95–P5 elevation range.
  • Median interior slope.
  • RMS relief residual after plane fitting.
  • Standardization using Earth-only median and interquartile range.
  • K-nearest-neighbor-style comparative ranking.

The system evaluates terrestrial locations against selected lunar and Martian reference environments. These rankings are exploratory screening results rather than proof of geological or environmental equivalence.

Technology Stack

  • Python: scientific data processing and backend analysis.
  • JavaScript and Vite: application interface.
  • CesiumJS: interactive 3D Earth visualization.
  • Three.js: planetary 3D visualization.
  • Gemini API: structured interpretation and organization of evidence.
  • NASA and other open geospatial datasets: scientific reference information.

Discovery Experiments and Results

The project includes an initial discovery experiment that generated 49 geographic grid centers. Of these, 26 were evaluated as eligible candidates, while 23 were excluded based on screening criteria.

Additional independent discovery experiments expanded the candidate catalogs to 64 and 69 locations. These experiments preserve separate candidate populations and calibration procedures.

The platform also includes five regional investigation windows, covering South American study areas and an East African water-screening control region.

Scientific Limitations

Eksoterris is an exploratory research tool. Topographic similarity alone does not establish that a terrestrial location is a validated planetary analog.

Additional geological, mineralogical, environmental, and field evidence is necessary to establish stronger scientific conclusions. Some evidence layers remain unavailable or unverified.

Expected Impact

Eksoterris seeks to make planetary analog investigation more accessible, visual, and reproducible by connecting geospatial datasets with interactive exploration and comparative analysis.

The platform provides a foundation for future research involving geological evidence, environmental conditions, remote sensing, and the identification of terrestrial locations that may support planetary exploration studies.

Team: ICAMIABAS
Challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Exploring Earth to better understand other worlds.
